summary: Requires the Secretary of the Interior to partner with the Secretary of Agriculture and Hawaii to continue research on Rapid Ohia Death transmission vectors, manage ungulates in affected areas, and fund forest restoration and research to prevent spread of the fungal disease.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture to continue research, ungulate management, financial assistance, forest restoration, and infrastructure funding to address Rapid Ohia Death. This explicitly sustains and requires ongoing federal expenditures on these activities, pushing the bill toward expanded government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses a fungal disease in native Hawaiian trees and has no connection to human healthcare systems or policy.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions address immigration, borders, or related pathways.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military, defense, or national security spending.

The bill mandates federal collaboration to research disease transmission, manage ungulates, prevent spread of Rapid Ohia Death, and restore native Hawaiian forests. This directly expands environmental protection and restoration efforts on federal, state, and private lands.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No provisions relate to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions relate to trade, tariffs, or globalization.

The bill requires sustained federal financial assistance and infrastructure funding without any offsetting revenue measures, which implicitly accepts additional deficit spending rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions relate to foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.
No provisions relate to technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight of tech companies.
No provisions relate to worker protections, unions, or employer flexibility.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or civil rights protections.
